newsitem.title: USA: U.S. denies trying to help overthrow Sudan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. denies trying to help overthrow Sudan.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was sending military aid to Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda but denied it was assisting those countries in a bid to help overthrow Sudan's militant Islamic regime.

The Washington Post, quoting unnamed officials, reported on Sunday the United States was about to send $20 million in surplus military equipment to Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda, which are abetting Sudanese opposition groups preparing a joint offensive to topple the regime in Khartoum.
State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies, at a news briefing on Tuesday, acknowledged Washington was supplying "nonlethal defensive military assistance" to the three countries.
But he insisted: "We are not seeking the overthrow of the government in Khartoum."
"The issue of the future of the government in Khartoum is up to the Sudanese people, it's not for us to try to affect that," he said.
Davies noted that the United States maintained diplomatic relations with Sudan and has "an active dialogue" with the government there.

But he also stressed that "we continue to view Sudanese support for terrorism and its support for groups that seek to destabilise neighbouring states as a threat to U.S. interests, and we continue to raise that with the government in Khartoum."

The Post quoted officials as saying all of the aid was non-lethal, including radios, uniforms, boots and tents. But the newspaper also quoted congressional and Pentagon sources as saying this could be expanded to include rifles and other weapons.
